DNS & LB Lookup

Resolve a list of host names or IPs against your configured DNS servers and, in the same step, find which FortiWeb server policy or FortiADC virtual server publishes them — with links to the policy, DNS record management and a guarded service decommission.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsnetwork.view users.manage operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereOperations → DNS Lookup (Global, FortiWeb, FortiADC) (URL /dns-lookup/)

What is it?#

DNS & LB Lookup takes up to 50 host names or IP addresses and answers two questions at once:

  1. What does DNS say? — each entry is resolved with dig against every DNS server configured for this site.
  2. Who publishes it? — each entry is matched against the load-balancing configuration of the fleet: FortiWeb server policies (from SATOM's cache) and FortiADC virtual servers (read live).

From a match you can open the policy, manage DNS records in an external DNS backend, or decommission the whole service.

What does it do?#

  • Resolves each entry against each enabled DNS server (A by default; reverse lookup for IPs; name TYPE for another type such as CNAME). A wildcard *.example.com is probed as example.example.com.
  • Shows LB matches: product, gateway, ADOM, policy/virtual server, service IP, HTTP/HTTPS service, pool, members, certificate CN, SNI, WAF policy, App ID, comment, status, zone, line, department — plus a mini path policy → pool → backends coloured by configured status.
  • Quick LB shows only the gateway(s).
  • Copy DNS / Copy LB copy tab-separated results for a spreadsheet.
  • Lists entries Not found in any source.
  • DNS Records (administrators) — list, create, edit and delete records in a configured DNS backend (EfficientIP SOLIDserver, phpIPAM or NetBox).
  • Decommission — plan and execute the removal of a service: its DNS records, the server policy / virtual server, SNI membership, certificate, WAF profile and carve-outs, with a preview first.

Requirements#

  • At least one DNS server configured in Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Lookup (none are shipped). Until then the page says No DNS servers configured.
  • For FortiWeb matches: harvested configuration (the page reads the cache).
  • For DNS Records: a DNS backend in Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Records.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

  • Lookup (opening the page): network.view; all system profiles have it. Without it the sidebar link is hidden and the page answers 403. Results are limited to the appliances of the current ADOM (Global sees all).
  • Manage in Settings → DNS Lookup (the server list) and DNS Records: users.manage (Administrator). The button and link are hidden otherwise; the endpoints return 403.
  • Decommission: the legacy config_write gate (e.g. operations.apply or appliances.apply); the button only appears for FortiWeb and FortiADC matches.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: DNS & LB Lookup now requires network.view instead of sign-in alone.

How to use#

Look up names#

  1. Open Operations → DNS Lookup.
  2. Paste entries into Hostnames / IPs — one per line (optionally name TYPE).
  3. Choose Options: Show LB matches (default on), Quick LB (gateway only), Exact match, Show TTL.
  4. Click Search. Reset clears the form.
  5. Expand a match to see the details; Open policy opens the FortiWeb policy in a new tab.

Manage DNS records (administrators)#

  1. Click DNS Records in the Results header.
  2. Choose the Backend (if several are configured), enter Name (FQDN), Zone, View as offered by the backend, and click Load.
  3. Edit a record or fill Type, Value, TTL and click Save record; New clears the form. Delete from the list.

Decommission a service#

  1. On a match, click Decommission. SATOM builds a plan: every object that would be deleted, kept or unbound, with warnings.
  2. Read the plan. If it carries warnings, tick I have read the warnings above and accept the shared dependencies they name.
  3. Type the policy name in type the policy name to confirm.
  4. Click Delete everything listed. Results are shown per object.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Hostnames / IPs One per line; characters outside letters, digits, space and . : * _ - / are removed; max 50 entries Yes www.example.com
Show LB matches Match each entry against LB configuration No on
Quick LB (gateway only) Show only the gateway column No off
Exact match Whole-value (or comma-separated token) match instead of substring No off
Show TTL Append (TTL:n) to DNS answers No off

DNS servers (Settings → DNS Lookup): a list of name + server address with an enabled flag.

Example#

🧪Example — Who serves api.example.com, and retire it

  1. Enter api.example.com, keep Show LB matches, click Search.
  2. Both DNS servers return 192.0.2.40; one match shows FortiWeb fweb-01, policy pol-api, pool pool-api with two backends.
  3. Click Decommission: the plan lists the A record, the policy, its pool, the certificate (keep — also used by another policy), and the WAF profile.
  4. Type pol-api and click Delete everything listed.

Result#

  • Lookups change nothing and are not audited.
  • DNS record changes write audit entries dns_records.create, .update, .delete.
  • Every decommission attempt writes dns_decommission.apply (successful or refused). Objects are deleted in this order: DNS records, server policy / virtual server, SNI, certificate, WAF policy, carve-outs. If the policy itself fails to delete, nothing after it is attempted.

Troubleshooting#

403 when opening DNS Lookup, or the link is missing#

Your profile does not hold network.view. Ask an administrator to add it.

"No DNS servers configured."#

Add servers under Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Lookup (administrators).

"LB matching failed: …"#

Building LB rows failed; the DNS half still shows. Check the devices and the cache (see Device health).

A DNS cell shows "timeout", "error" or "No result"#

The server did not answer within the timeout, the query failed, or there is no record. Check the server address in Settings.

"the plan changed since you saw it — review it again before confirming."#

Something changed between preview and confirmation (for example another session bound the certificate elsewhere). Review the new plan and confirm again.

"this plan carries warnings that need an explicit acknowledgement."#

Tick the acknowledgement checkbox.

"this plan is blocked and cannot be acknowledged away."#

A blocker (for example an object that could not be read) prevents deletion. Objects SATOM could not verify are always kept, never deleted.

"the server policy did not delete — the rest of the plan was not attempted."#

The appliance refused the policy deletion; nothing else was removed after it. See the per-object results for the reason.

"No backend carries the DNS role. Configure one in Settings -> DNS Records."#

No DNS backend is configured for record management.

"N DNS backends are configured — say which one this record belongs to."#

Choose the Backend in the dialog.

Advanced#

Advanced Data sources and matching
  • FortiWeb LB rows come from the device cache (no device call); FortiADC rows are read live, read-only.
  • Matching compares the entry and its wildcard-resolved form against every column of every LB row (substring by default).
  • The App ID column is taken from the policy/virtual-server comment (AppID: <token>, app-id=…, or a bracketed [APP-123]).
  • dig runs with a 2-second timeout and one try per server; lookups run in parallel (up to 8).
#dns#dig#lookup#hostname#load balancer match#vip#decommission#dns records#efficientip#phpipam#netbox
